priorStories.headline: U.S. economy grew at a 3.4% annual rate
priorStories.body:
The U.S. economy expanded at an annualized 3.4% in the third quarter, according to the government’s initial estimate, accelerating from 2.2% in the second quarter.

Inflation remained elevated in September. The personal consumption expenditures price index rose 3.6% from a year earlier, while the measure excluding food and energy rose 3.1%. Both reports are subject to revision.

priorStories.headline: Israeli election leaves no bloc a majority
priorStories.body:
Israel’s completed vote count gave Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc 53 of the Knesset’s 120 seats, short of the 61 needed for a majority. The main opposition won 48 seats, and Arab-led parties won 19.

The results remain subject to certification and submission to President Isaac Herzog, leaving the next government unresolved.

priorStories.headline: U.S. completes 172-million-barrel oil release
priorStories.body:
The Energy Department awarded contracts to exchange more than 40 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, completing a planned 172-million-barrel emergency release.

The contracts require more than 216 million barrels to be returned to the reserve beginning in 2027.

candidates.summary: Russian and Ukrainian officials participating in a humanitarian mission entered Russian-occupied Oleshky in southern Ukraine. Ukrainian ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said the convoy was bringing food, medical supplies and other aid to residents under a localized ceasefire.
candidates.title: Humanitarian mission enters Russian-occupied Oleshky

candidates.summary: Qatari mediators returned to Tehran as part of U.S.-coordinated efforts to negotiate an agreement between Iran and the United States, an official briefed on the talks told Reuters. The sides remained divided over whether nuclear issues or an end to the U.S. port blockade and oil sanctions should come first.
candidates.title: Qatari mediators return to Tehran for U.S.-Iran talks
